title: Coupling Dy3 Triangles Enhances Their Slow Magnetic Relaxation

material_class.structural_family: two Tm3 triangles linked by a double alkoxide bridge from reduced o-vanillin

synthesis.procedure: To a stirred solution of o-vanillin (152 mg, 1.0 mmol), furfurylamine (98 mg, 1.0 mmol) and triethylamine (101 mg, 1.0 mmol) in methanol (40 mL) was added TmCl3·6H2O (383 mg, 1.0 mmol). The solution was refluxed for 2 h, cooled and filtered. Slow evaporation of the yellow solution for over 2 weeks gave yellow block crystals. One o-vanillinate per triangle is reduced to the alkoxide L′, which doubly bridges two Tm3 triangles.
synthesis.time: 2 h reflux, then slow evaporation for over 2 weeks
synthesis.vessel_or_method: stirred methanol solution, reflux, filtration, slow evaporation
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Cooled and filtered; slow evaporation of the yellow solution for over 2 weeks yielded X-ray quality yellow block crystals.

source_locations.location: structure discussion of the linked triangles

material_class.structural_family: two Dy3 triangles linked by a double alkoxide bridge; 1:1 terminal Cl/H2O disorder

synthesis.procedure: Method 1: A methanolic solution of 2-hydroxy-3-methoxybenzyl alcohol (77 mg, 0.5 mmol) and triethylamine (101 mg, 1.0 mmol) in methanol (20 mL) was added to o-vanillin (76 mg, 0.5 mmol), furfurylamine (48 mg, 0.5 mmol) and triethylamine (50 mg, 0.5 mmol) in methanol (20 mL). DyCl3·6H2O (376 mg, 1.0 mmol) was added with stirring. The mixture was refluxed for 2 h, cooled and filtered. Slow evaporation of the yellow solution for over 2 weeks gave yellow block crystals. Method 2 repeats Method 1 without furfurylamine and gives a lower yield. An excess of the alcohol ligand is required to suppress formation of the Dy3 triangle.
synthesis.time: 2 h reflux, then slow evaporation for over 2 weeks
synthesis.vessel_or_method: stirred methanol solution, reflux, filtration, slow evaporation
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Cooled and filtered; slow evaporation of the yellow solution for over 2 weeks yielded X-ray quality yellow block crystals.

properties.summary: Dy6 is a single-molecule magnet with two zero-field relaxation processes (χ'' maxima near 25 K and 5 K). Linking the Dy3 triangles raises the temperature of slow relaxation relative to the parent triangle (about 8 K to 25 K). Room-temperature χT matches six noninteracting DyIII ions; low-T susceptibility shows weak antiferromagnetic coupling that is overcome by a moderate field. Magnetization reaches a plateau near 28 μB. High-temperature Arrhenius parameters are ΔE = 200(10) K and τ0 = 1.5(5)×10−9 s, with deviation from Arrhenius behavior on cooling. A 1 kOe static field has little effect on the dynamics. Ab initio and single-crystal magnetometry indicate a nonmagnetic ground doublet and a temperature-dependent change of anisotropy associated with the broken trigonal symmetry.
